primitives.name: Fractional Tackle Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our approach first identifies when a defender is in a "contact window" of the ball-carrier during a play, before assigning value to each window and the players involved.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_ij': 'Fractional tackle value for contact window j in play i, dimensionless', 'v_start_ij': 'Initial velocity of ball-carrier at start of window j in play i, yards/second', 'v_end_ij': 'Final velocity of ball-carrier at end of window j in play i, yards/second', 'v_pre_ij': 'Peak velocity of ball-carrier prior to window j in play i, yards/second'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball-carrier velocity is measured continuously; contact windows are temporally defined; defenders' contributions are linearly additive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When v_pre_ij = 0 or v_end_ij > v_pre_ij, fractional value becomes undefined or zero.

primitives.name: Contact Window Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our approach first identifies when a defender is in a "contact window" of the ball-carrier during a play, before assigning value to each window and the players involved.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W_j^i': 'Set of time frames constituting contact window j in play i, seconds', 'T_i': 'Time interval of play i, seconds', 'd_defender,t': 'Distance between defender and ball-carrier at time t, feet', 'r_contact': 'Threshold distance defining contact proximity, feet'}

primitives.name: Defensive Contribution Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: This enables us to devise a new metric called fractional tackles, which credits defenders for halting the ball-carrier's forward motion toward the end zone.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_k^i': 'Total fractional tackle score for defender k in play i, dimensionless', 'W_k^i': 'Set of contact windows involving defender k in play i, seconds', 'w_kj': 'Fractional tackle value for window j involving defender k, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Each defender’s contribution is additive across contact windows; attribution is proportional to time spent in contact.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Zero attribution if no contact windows exist or if all values are non-positive.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's influence propagation model, aggregating contact window impacts into cumulative defensive effect.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative velocity suppression per defender, derived from NGS velocity traces.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in transforming discrete, subjective tackling records into a continuous, objective measure using player tracking data. The framework defines a 'contact window' as a temporal interval where a defender is within proximity to the ball-carrier. Within this window, the fractional tackle value is calculated as the ratio of velocity lost during the contact to the pre-contact peak velocity. This formulation allows for nuanced attribution of defensive effort even when tackles are not officially recorded. The derivation uses a normalized difference in velocities to quantify impact, ensuring that partial stops contribute proportionally. The method avoids binary outcomes typical of solo/assist tackles by treating each moment of contact as a continuous variable. It also introduces corrections for edge cases such as recovery of velocity post-contact or pre-existing peak velocity. These refinements allow for a more granular and accurate representation of defensive performance, especially for players who lack traditional tackle statistics.
